Put your GPU to work on FLOP

Today FLOP runs only as a development network (devnet). Nothing here involves real money yet, and this page does not promise future earnings.

FLOP is a network where AI agents pay for answers from AI models. A GPU machine on FLOP runs a model, answers those requests, and produces evidence that it ran the exact model it claims. FLOP calls the person running such a machine a miner, whether the GPU is owned or rented. You do not need to know crypto to start: this page explains the few parts that work like crypto. When you are ready for commands, Run a FLOP miner on a GPU host has the full setup.

What your machine does

It runs two programs in Docker on one NVIDIA GPU machine:

  • a model server, which runs the AI model on the GPU;
  • a worker, which takes requests from the network, records evidence of the work, and reports it.

Before real requests arrive, the network measures how much work the machine actually delivers. This calibration takes from under an hour to several hours, depending on the network's current settings, and is renewed every week. Keep the machine running: a test job left unanswered past its deadline is penalized.

The crypto parts, in plain words

  • Account. A secret key identifies your machine on the network and receives its pay. It lives in a protected file on the machine. Never paste it into a chat, an email, or a conversation with an AI assistant; nobody at FLOP will ask for it.
  • FLOP. The network's own currency. Requests are paid in FLOP.
  • Deposit (stake). While the machine serves, its account must lock some FLOP. A faster machine locks more, because it can take on more work. Part of the deposit can be taken away (slashed) if the machine misbehaves, for example by leaving jobs unanswered. On the devnet, FLOP's devnet operator provides this FLOP; the public faucet does not cover it.

Which hardware works

  • An NVIDIA GPU server you own, or a rented virtual machine (VM) with a GPU, where you can run Docker with GPU access. Container-only rentals that do not allow Docker inside will not work.
  • The tested setup is an NVIDIA A40 running a small model (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct). Other NVIDIA cards may work, but each needs its own check first.
  • Enough disk for the model, and a machine that stays on.
  • For rentals, GPU.ai VMs are the documented option. A RunPod GPU Pod can run the model, with the rest of the miner on a separate small server. Stopping the programs does not stop rental billing: delete the machine at the provider when you are done.

The full checklist is under Choose a host in Run a FLOP miner on a GPU host.

How to start

  1. Join the devnet over its public endpoints. No invitation is needed: Join the devnet in Run a FLOP miner on a GPU host lists the endpoints, the automatic stake sponsor and its limits.
  2. Follow Run a FLOP miner on a GPU host, or let an AI coding agent do it: that page's Set up with your agent section has the install command and what to ask.
